protocol: Farnborough. A 34-year-old pilot had an initial hypoxia demonstration at 28,000 ft. Oxygen was resumed and joint pain was recorded on ascent through 32,000 ft. Maximum pressure altitude is unavailable.
outcome_window: During the chamber exposure through recovery. Delayed visual, motor and cognitive signs followed descent.
locator: Fryer 1969, printed pp. 130–131 (PDF pp. 127–128), neurological Case 17
note: The source cites Roxburgh 1953 for this historical case. Early hand spasms occurred during the hypoxia demonstration. Approximate delay to the later neurological phase is recorded separately. The author reports hospitalization, seizure and later neurological recovery.

protocol: A 33-year-old pilot took part in a training chamber demonstration including 25,000 ft followed by 37,000 ft. The report describes two earlier uneventful demonstrations.
outcome_window: During chamber ascent and descent through hospital recovery. The first witnessed generalized seizure occurred on the following evening.
locator: Fryer 1969, printed pp. 131–134 (PDF pp. 128–131), neurological Case 18
note: Fryer describes a case he observed. Acute hypoxia was part of the training, followed by pain and delayed neurological deterioration. The source reports a probable decompression relationship and eventual complete recovery.
